sentences.text:
Heard Mr. Rajeev Kumar Singh, the learned counsel for applicant, the learned Aga for
State-opposite party no. 1 and Mr. Vinay Kumar Singh, Advocate who has put in apperance on
behalf of prosecutrix-opposite party no. 5 by filing of a short counter affidavit along with his
vakalatnama in Court today, which is taken on record.
2. Perused the record.

3. Applicant-Rajesh Gaur, who is a charge sheeted accused, and facing trail before court below has approached this Court by means of present application under Section 528 BNS with the following prayer:-

Rajesh Gaur) arising out of Case Crime No. 107/2019 U/s -363, 366, 376, 120-B I.P.C. and Section-3/4 POCSO Act and Section-3(2)5 SC/ST Act, Police Station-Jhangaha, District-Gorakhpur including the Charge Sheet No. 02/2019 dated 04.07.2019 as well as cognizance and summoning order dated 30.07.2020 as well as consequential orders as like order of N.B.W. dated 30.07.2024 on words passed by the Court of Additional Session Judge/Special Judge (POCSO Act), Court No. 1 Gorakhpur pending in the court of Additional Session Judge/Special Judge (POCSO Act), Court No. 2 Gorakhpur,
during the pendency of the present case before this Hon'ble court.
And/or to pass such other and further order which this Hon'ble court may deem fit and proper under the circumstances of the case."
4.

entities.text: Additional Session Judge/Special Judge (POCSO Act), Court No. 2 Gorakhpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicant submits that though applicant is a named and charge sheeted accused and also facing trial before the court below, however, in view of the subsequent developments that have emerged on record, the criminal prosecution of the applicant cannot be sustained any further.
As such, the present application is liable to be allowed.

5. In futherance of aforesaid submission, the learned counsel for applicant submits that criminal prosecution of applicant was set in notion, when an FIR dated 4.4.2019 was lodged by the first informant-opposite party no. 2 Smt. Ghoorpati (mother of the prosecutix) and was registered as Case Crime No. 0107 of 2019, under Section 363, 366 IPC, P.S. Jhangaha, District Gorakhpur.
In the aforesaid FIR, one Vikas has been nominated as named accused.
6. However, during pendency of aforementioned criminal case, the named accused Vikas solemnized marriage with prosecutrix in the year 2019 in accordance with Hindu rites and custom.

Subsequently, named accused Vikas was acquitted of the charges alleged against him vide judgment and order dated 6.10.2020 passed by concern Juvenile Justice Board in Case No. 121 of 2019 (State vs. Vikas Gaur), under Section 363, 366, 376 IPC and 3/4 POCSO Act and Section 3(2)(V) of SC/ST Act, P.S. Jhangaha, District Gorakhpur.

sentences.text: On the above conspectus, the learned counsel for applicants submits that in view of the aforementioned subsequent developments that have taken place, the criminality, if any, committed by applicant now stands washed of.
As such, no useful purpose shall be served in prolonging the criminal prosecution of applicant.

In view of the fact that co-accused who is the brother of present applicant has solemnized marriage with the prosecutrix, and has also been acquitted of the charges alleged against him the chances of conviction of present applicant are not only remote but also bleak.
As such no useful purpose shall now be served in prolonging the criminal prosecution of applicant.
On the above premise, it is thus urged by the learned counsel for applicant that present application is liable to be allowed by this Court.

8. Learned counsel for the applicant has the invited attention of court to the judgment of Supreme Court in Case of in K. Dhandapani Vs. State by the Inspector of Police, 2022 SCC OnLine SC 1056 and Mafat Lal and others Vs. State of Rajasthan, (2022) 6 SCC 589, wherein the Apex Court quashed the proceedings against the accused therein on the ground that he has solemnized marriage with the prosecutrix and Court cannot turn a blind eye to the said fact.

entities.text: K. Dhandapani Vs. State by the Inspector of Police, 2022 SCC OnLine SC 1056
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Mafat Lal and others Vs. State of Rajasthan, (2022) 6 SCC 589
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
On the facts as stated above,
learned counsel for applicant thus submits that the ratio laid down by Apex Court in aforementioned judgments is squarely applicable to the facts of the present case also as the brother of the applicant has solemnized marriage with the prosecutrix.
As such, no exception can be carved out in respect of aforementioned judgments of the Supreme Court in so far as the applicant is concerned.

9. On the above premise, learned counsel for the applicant thus, submits that this Court while exercising jurisdiction under Section 482 Cr.P.C. should not ignore the subsequent developments that have taken place.
As such, the present application is liable to be allowed.
10. Per contra, the learned AGA representing State-opposite party 1 has vehemently opposed the present application.

However, he could not dispute the facts that the named and charge sheeted accused Vikas has already been acquitted by the concerned Juvenile Justice Board and further aforesaid accused has solemnized marriage with the prosecutrix.
11. On the other hand, Mr. Vinay Kumar Singh, the learned counsel representing the prosecutrix/victim-opposite party no. 5 does not oppose the present application.
He submits that he has received instructions not to oppose the present application.
According to learned counsel representing opposite party no. 5, it is now an admitted fact that Vikas the brother of present applicant has solemnized marriage with the prosecutrix.
By reason of above, the prosecutrix is residing with Vikas the brother of the applicant as his legally wedded wife.
He therefore, contends that he cannot have any objection in case the present application is decided by this Court, taking into consideration aforementioned facts.

12. Having heard the learned counsel for applicant, the learned AGA for State-opposite party no. 1,
Mr. Vinay Kumar Singh, the learned counsel representing prosecutrix/victim-opposite party 5 and on perusal of record, this Court find that the matter requires consideration.

13. Notice on behalf of State opposite party-1 has been accepted by the learned A.G.A.

14. Issue notice to first informant/opposite party no. 2.
15.

Mr. Vinay Kumar Singh, Advocate has put in appearance on behalf of prosecutrix/opposite party no. 5.
16.
All the opposite parties may file their respective counter affidavits within four weeks.
Applicant will have two weeks thereafter to file his rejoinder affidavit.

17. List this application for admission on 30.5.2025.
18.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also the submissions urged by the learned counsel for applicant in support of this application as noted herein above, as an interim measure, it is, hereby, provided that until further orders of this Court, further proceedings in Session Case No. 597/2020 (State Vs. Rajesh Gaur) arising out of Case Crime No. 107/2019 U/s -363, 366, 376, 120-B I.P.C. and Section-3/4 POCSO Act and Section-3(2)5 SC/ST Act, Police Station-Jhangaha, District-Gorakhpur now pending in the court of Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (POCSO Act), Court No. 2 Gorakhpur shall remain stayed.
